entries.title: Mathematics
entries.summary: The study of quantity, structure, space, change, and mathematical reasoning. Foundations sit inside this map; the other fields unfold around them.

entries.title: Foundations
entries.summary: The languages, assumptions, and methods that let mathematics make precise claims.

entries.title: Arithmetic
entries.summary: Numbers, operations, and the passage from counting to general numerical systems.

entries.title: Algebra
entries.summary: Equations and structures governed by operations, symmetry, and transformations.

entries.title: Numbers & number theory
entries.summary: Divisibility, prime numbers, and arithmetic patterns in integers and larger number systems.

entries.title: Calculus & analysis
entries.summary: Limits, continuity, differentiation, integration, and infinite processes.

entries.title: Geometry & topology
entries.summary: Shapes and spaces, from Euclidean measurements to curved and algebraic spaces.

entries.title: Topology
entries.summary: Continuity, connectedness, holes, and properties invariant under homeomorphism.

entries.title: Discrete mathematics
entries.summary: Counting, finite structures, networks, order, and combinatorial existence.

entries.title: Probability
entries.summary: Mathematical models of randomness, distributions, and stochastic evolution.

entries.title: Statistics
entries.summary: Learning about populations and models from incomplete, variable observations.

entries.title: Differential equations
entries.summary: Equations for unknown functions and the evolving systems they describe.

entries.title: Optimization
entries.summary: Finding best feasible choices and understanding the geometry of decisions.

entries.title: Computation & optimization
entries.summary: Algorithms, computability, complexity, and reliable numerical approximation.

entries.title: Information & coding
entries.summary: Quantifying uncertainty, transmitting information, and protecting mathematical communication.

entries.title: Mathematical physics
entries.summary: Mathematical structures for mechanics, fields, quantum theory, and spacetime.

entries.title: Set theory
entries.summary: Collections, membership, constructions, and the sizes of infinite sets.

entries.title: Set operations
entries.summary: Union, intersection, difference, and complement construct new sets from given sets.
entries.formula: A ∩ B = {x : x ∈ A and x ∈ B}
entries.condition: Intersection keeps precisely the common elements.

entries.title: Relations
entries.summary: A relation records which ordered pairs satisfy a specified condition.
entries.condition: A binary relation from A to B is a subset of their Cartesian product.

entries.title: Functions & relations
entries.summary: Functions assign one output to every input in their domain.

entries.title: Equivalence relations
entries.summary: Reflexive, symmetric, transitive relations partition a set into equivalence classes.

entries.title: Cardinality
entries.summary: Bijections compare the sizes of finite and infinite sets.
entries.formula: A ∼ B ⇔ there exists a bijection A → B
entries.condition: Equal cardinality does not require the sets to have identical elements.

entries.title: Countability
entries.summary: A set is countable when it is finite or can be listed by the natural numbers.

entries.title: Ordinals
entries.summary: Ordinals describe order types of well-ordered sets and support transfinite induction.

entries.title: ZFC axioms
entries.summary: A widely used axiomatic framework specifies which set constructions are available.

entries.title: Axiom of choice
entries.summary: A choice function selects an element from each member of a family of nonempty sets.

entries.title: Continuum hypothesis
entries.summary: The question asks whether a cardinal size lies strictly between the integers and the real numbers.

entries.title: Mathematical logic
entries.summary: Formal languages and the relationships between truth, proofs, and mathematical models.

entries.title: Propositional logic
entries.summary: Combine truth-valued statements using connectives such as conjunction and implication.

entries.title: First-order logic
entries.summary: Quantifiers range over individuals in a structure, while predicates express their properties.

entries.title: Quantifiers
entries.summary: Universal and existential quantifiers distinguish claims about every object from claims about some object.

entries.title: Model theory
entries.summary: Study structures satisfying formal theories and what their languages can express.

entries.title: Proof theory
entries.summary: Treat formal proofs as mathematical objects and study their transformations and strength.

entries.title: Gödel’s completeness theorem
entries.summary: Every logically valid first-order sentence is provable in a complete proof system.

entries.title: Incompleteness theorems
entries.summary: Sufficiently expressive consistent effectively axiomatized arithmetic theories cannot decide every arithmetic sentence.

entries.title: Nonclassical logics
entries.summary: Alternative logical systems change principles such as excluded middle or the treatment of modality.

entries.title: Proof methods
entries.summary: Ways to establish a statement from assumptions, rather than infer it from a few examples.

entries.title: Direct proof
entries.summary: Deduce a conclusion by applying definitions and known results to the assumptions.

entries.title: Proof by contradiction
entries.summary: Assume the negation of a claim and derive a contradiction with accepted assumptions.

entries.title: Contrapositive
entries.summary: Prove an implication by showing that the failure of its conclusion forces failure of its premise.
entries.condition: This equivalence uses classical propositional logic.

entries.title: Mathematical induction
entries.summary: A base case and an inductive step establish a statement over the natural numbers.

entries.title: Strong induction
entries.summary: An inductive step may use all earlier cases rather than just the immediately previous one.

entries.title: Structural induction
entries.summary: Prove properties of recursively built objects by following their construction rules.

entries.title: Counterexamples
entries.summary: One example violating a universal statement disproves that statement.

entries.title: Constructive proof
entries.summary: Establish existence by giving a construction or an effective way to obtain the object.

entries.title: Category theory
entries.summary: Objects and composable arrows reveal common structure across different mathematical fields.

entries.title: Categories & morphisms
entries.summary: A category has objects, identity arrows, and associative composition of arrows.

entries.title: Functors
entries.summary: A functor maps objects and arrows between categories while preserving identities and composition.

entries.title: Natural transformations
entries.summary: Compatible arrow families compare two functors without choosing coordinates.

entries.title: Universal properties
entries.summary: Characterize an object through the unique ways other objects map to or from it.

entries.title: Limits & colimits
entries.summary: Universal constructions collect compatible diagrams or glue their data together.

entries.title: Adjoint functors
entries.summary: An adjunction relates two functors through a natural correspondence between morphism sets.

entries.title: Yoneda lemma
entries.summary: An object can be understood through all morphisms into it, in a precise functorial sense.

entries.title: Topos theory
entries.summary: Categories with set-like structure connect geometry, sheaves, and internal logic.

entries.title: Type theory
entries.summary: Types organize mathematical expressions and support foundations based on construction and computation.

entries.title: Simple type theory
entries.summary: Assign types to expressions so function application respects input and output types.

entries.title: Dependent types
entries.summary: A type may depend on a value, allowing statements and their evidence to be encoded together.

entries.title: Curry–Howard correspondence
entries.summary: Proofs correspond to programs, and propositions to types, in suitable formal systems.

entries.title: Lambda calculus
entries.summary: Function abstraction and application form a minimal language of computation.

entries.title: Homotopy type theory
entries.summary: Interpret identities as paths and relate dependent types to homotopy-theoretic spaces.

entries.title: Proof assistants
entries.summary: Computer systems check formal proof steps against explicitly specified logical rules.

entries.title: Axiomatic systems
entries.summary: Axioms and inference rules specify the starting points and allowed deductions of a theory.

entries.title: Power sets
entries.summary: The power set contains every subset of a given set.
entries.condition: A subset of B is an element of B’s power set.

entries.title: Cartesian products
entries.summary: Ordered pairs let two sets form a common product space.
entries.formula: A × B = {(a,b) : a ∈ A, b ∈ B}
entries.condition: Order matters: (a,b) need not equal (b,a).

entries.title: Injective functions
entries.summary: Different inputs always produce different outputs.

entries.title: Surjective functions
entries.summary: Every element of the declared codomain is attained by some input.

entries.title: Bijections & inverses
entries.summary: A function is bijective when it is both injective and surjective, and then has an inverse.

entries.title: Function composition
entries.summary: The output of one function becomes the input of another.
entries.condition: The image of f must lie in the domain of g.

entries.title: Number systems
entries.summary: Extend counting numbers to systems that support subtraction, division, limits, and algebraic equations.

entries.title: Natural numbers
entries.summary: Counting numbers support addition, multiplication, and mathematical induction.

entries.title: Integers & divisibility
entries.summary: Adjoin negative numbers so subtraction is always possible.

entries.title: Rational numbers
entries.summary: Ratios of integers support division by nonzero elements.
entries.condition: Different ratios can represent the same rational number.

entries.title: Real numbers
entries.summary: A complete ordered field models a continuous number line.

entries.title: Complex numbers
entries.summary: Adjoin i with i² = −1, and represent numbers as points of a plane.

entries.title: Quaternions
entries.summary: A four-dimensional real algebra has noncommutative multiplication and represents spatial rotations.

entries.title: p-adic numbers
entries.summary: A number system uses divisibility by a fixed prime to define closeness.

entries.title: Arithmetic operations
entries.summary: Operations on numbers and the rules that govern their manipulation.

entries.title: Addition
entries.summary: Combine quantities using an operation whose neutral element is zero.

entries.title: Subtraction
entries.summary: Subtracting b reverses adding b when additive inverses exist.

entries.title: Multiplication
entries.summary: Repeated addition extends to a distributive operation on broader number systems.

entries.title: Division
entries.summary: Division by a nonzero number reverses multiplication where a multiplicative inverse exists.

entries.title: Exponentiation
entries.summary: Repeated multiplication extends through roots, real powers, and complex exponentials.

entries.title: Logarithms
entries.summary: A logarithm recovers an exponent from the corresponding power.
entries.condition: For real logarithms require a > 0, a ≠ 1, x > 0, and y > 0.

entries.title: Fractions & ratios
entries.summary: Fractions express equal parts or ratios, while equivalent fractions describe the same quantity.

entries.title: Absolute value
entries.summary: The magnitude of a real number is its distance from zero.
entries.condition: This identity is for real x.

entries.title: Elementary algebra
entries.summary: Use variables, equations, inequalities, and functions to generalize arithmetic.

entries.title: Algebraic expressions
entries.summary: Variables and operations describe quantities without necessarily asserting an equality.

entries.title: Equations & polynomials
entries.summary: A solution makes the expressions on both sides of an equality agree.

entries.title: Inequalities
entries.summary: Order relations compare quantities and restrict sets of possible values.

entries.title: Linear equations
entries.summary: An equation is linear when unknowns appear only to the first degree without products between unknowns.

entries.title: Quadratic equations
entries.summary: Second-degree equations have roots governed by their discriminant.
entries.condition: For ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.

entries.title: Polynomials
entries.summary: Finite sums of nonnegative integer powers support evaluation, factorization, and division.

entries.title: Rational functions
entries.summary: A quotient of polynomials is defined where its denominator is nonzero.

entries.title: Exponential functions
entries.summary: Constant proportional growth produces an exponential dependence on the input.

entries.title: Linear algebra
entries.summary: Vector spaces, linear maps, matrices, and the structures that preserve addition and scaling.

entries.title: Vector spaces
entries.summary: Vectors admit addition and scalar multiplication over a field.

entries.title: Linear transformations
entries.summary: Linear maps preserve every linear combination.
entries.condition: This must hold for all vectors u,v and scalars a,b.

entries.title: Matrices
entries.summary: A matrix represents a linear map after input and output bases are chosen.

entries.title: Linear systems
entries.summary: Simultaneous linear equations describe an affine solution set when consistent.

entries.title: Inner product spaces
entries.summary: An inner product adds notions of angle and length to a vector space.

entries.title: Determinants
entries.summary: An alternating multilinear scalar detects invertibility and oriented volume scaling.

entries.title: Spectral theory
entries.summary: Eigenvalues and related decompositions reveal the action of linear operators.

entries.title: Tensors
entries.summary: Tensor products encode multilinear objects whose coordinate arrays depend on bases.

entries.title: Linear combinations
entries.summary: Add scalar multiples of vectors to construct new vectors.

entries.title: Linear span
entries.summary: The span is the smallest vector subspace containing a specified set of vectors.

entries.title: Linear independence
entries.summary: No vector in an independent finite list is a linear combination of the others.

entries.title: Bases & dimension
entries.summary: A basis is an independent spanning family; its cardinality is the dimension.

entries.title: Subspaces
entries.summary: A nonempty subset closed under addition and scalar multiplication is itself a vector space.

entries.title: Dual spaces
entries.summary: The dual consists of scalar-valued linear functions on a vector space.

entries.title: Change of basis
entries.summary: A coordinate change alters a representation while leaving the underlying vector or map unchanged.

entries.title: Kernel & image
entries.summary: The kernel records vectors mapped to zero; the image records attainable outputs.

entries.title: Rank–nullity theorem
entries.summary: The dimensions of the kernel and image add to the input dimension.
entries.formula: dim ker T + dim im T = dim V
entries.condition: V must be finite-dimensional.

entries.title: Linear isomorphisms
entries.summary: An invertible linear map identifies vector spaces while preserving their linear structure.

entries.title: Matrix multiplication
entries.summary: Multiplication represents composition and requires compatible dimensions.

entries.title: Transpose & adjoint
entries.summary: Transpose swaps matrix indices; the complex adjoint also conjugates entries.

entries.title: Matrix inverses
entries.summary: A square matrix is invertible exactly when its linear map is bijective.

entries.title: Matrix rank
entries.summary: Row rank and column rank agree and measure the dimension of the associated image.

entries.title: Matrix decompositions
entries.summary: Factor a matrix into structured components for understanding or computation.

entries.title: LU decomposition
entries.summary: Triangular factors support repeated solutions of linear systems, often with pivoting.

entries.title: QR decomposition
entries.summary: An orthogonal or unitary factor separates geometry from triangular coordinates.

entries.title: Singular value decomposition
entries.summary: Orthogonal input and output directions expose stretching factors of any rectangular matrix.
entries.condition: U and V are unitary; Σ has nonnegative singular values.

entries.title: Cholesky decomposition
entries.summary: A positive-definite Hermitian matrix factors as a triangular matrix times its adjoint.

entries.title: Jordan normal form
entries.summary: Over an algebraically closed field, generalized eigenvectors organize an operator into Jordan blocks.

entries.title: Euclidean vectors
entries.summary: A Euclidean vector represents a direction and magnitude in a flat inner product space.

entries.title: Orthogonality
entries.summary: Two vectors are orthogonal when their inner product is zero.

entries.title: Norms
entries.summary: A norm assigns a length compatible with scaling and the triangle inequality.

entries.title: Orthogonal projections
entries.summary: A closest-point projection splits a vector into a subspace component and an orthogonal remainder.

entries.title: Gram–Schmidt process
entries.summary: Successive orthogonalization turns an independent list into an orthonormal one.

entries.title: Eigenvalues
entries.summary: An eigenvalue is a scalar by which an operator stretches a nonzero eigenvector.

entries.title: Eigenvectors
entries.summary: An eigenvector preserves its direction under a linear map.
entries.condition: The zero vector is excluded from eigenvectors.

entries.title: Diagonalization
entries.summary: A basis of eigenvectors makes the matrix of a linear operator diagonal.

entries.title: Spectral theorem
entries.summary: Self-adjoint operators admit especially strong spectral decompositions under the relevant hypotheses.

entries.title: Positive-definite matrices
entries.summary: A Hermitian matrix is positive definite when its quadratic form is positive on every nonzero vector.

entries.title: Tensor products
entries.summary: A universal construction linearizes bilinear maps and combines vector spaces.

entries.title: Tensor contraction
entries.summary: Pair a vector index with a dual index and sum to reduce tensor order.

entries.title: Tensor eigenvalues
entries.summary: Higher-order tensors admit several inequivalent nonlinear spectral notions.

entries.title: CP decomposition
entries.summary: Express a tensor as a sum of rank-one outer products.

entries.title: Tucker decomposition
entries.summary: A core tensor links one factor space or matrix for each tensor mode.

entries.title: H-eigenvalues
entries.summary: For a real tensor, the eigen-equation uses componentwise powers on its right side.

entries.title: Z-eigenvalues
entries.summary: A normalized real eigenvector defines a different tensor eigenproblem from H-eigenvalues.

entries.title: M-eigenvalues
entries.summary: Coupled unit vectors produce spectral values for certain fourth-order elasticity tensors.

entries.title: Abstract algebra
entries.summary: Study operations through axioms rather than through particular numerical representations.

entries.title: Group theory
entries.summary: Groups capture associative composition with identities and inverses.

entries.title: Ring theory
entries.summary: Rings combine addition and multiplication linked by distributivity.

entries.title: Field theory
entries.summary: Fields allow addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by nonzero elements.

entries.title: Module theory
entries.summary: Modules generalize vector spaces by allowing scalars from a ring instead of a field.

entries.title: Representation theory
entries.summary: Represent abstract structures by linear transformations that preserve their operations.

entries.title: Universal algebra
entries.summary: Study algebraic operations and identities in a common language spanning many kinds of structures.

entries.title: Homological algebra
entries.summary: Chain complexes and derived constructions study algebraic information hidden in maps and relations.

entries.title: Subgroups
entries.summary: A subgroup is a subset that forms a group under the inherited operation.

entries.title: Group homomorphisms
entries.summary: Maps preserving multiplication compare groups and expose kernels and images.

entries.title: Normal subgroups
entries.summary: Invariance under conjugation is exactly what permits a quotient group construction.

entries.title: Quotient groups
entries.summary: Cosets of a normal subgroup form a group whose operation is induced from the original group.

entries.title: Group actions
entries.summary: A group acts by transformations on a set, organizing orbits and stabilizers.

entries.title: Permutation groups
entries.summary: Groups of bijections encode symmetries of finite or infinite sets.

entries.title: Cyclic groups
entries.summary: One element generates every group element by integer powers.

entries.title: Sylow theorems
entries.summary: Prime-power subgroup sizes constrain the structure of finite groups.

entries.title: Lie groups
entries.summary: A smooth manifold and a group structure coexist with smooth multiplication and inversion.

entries.title: Lie algebras
entries.summary: An antisymmetric bracket with the Jacobi identity describes infinitesimal symmetry.

entries.title: Exponential map
entries.summary: The exponential map relates a Lie algebra to one-parameter subgroups of its Lie group.

entries.title: Classical groups
entries.summary: Matrix groups preserve structures such as determinants, inner products, or symplectic forms.

entries.title: Ideals
entries.summary: An ideal is an additive subgroup closed under multiplication by arbitrary ring elements on the appropriate side.

entries.title: Quotient rings
entries.summary: Identify elements whose difference lies in an ideal to obtain a new ring.

entries.title: Polynomial rings
entries.summary: Adjoining formal variables extends coefficient arithmetic to polynomials.

entries.title: Integral domains
entries.summary: A commutative ring with unity and no zero divisors supports cancellation of nonzero factors.

entries.title: Unique factorization domains
entries.summary: Irreducible factorizations are unique up to order and multiplication by units.

entries.title: Noetherian rings
entries.summary: Ascending ideal chains stabilize, equivalently every ideal is finitely generated.

entries.title: Commutative algebra
entries.summary: Commutative rings and their modules supply the algebraic language of algebraic geometry.

entries.title: Field extensions
entries.summary: A larger field containing a smaller one can be studied as a vector space over the smaller field.

entries.title: Finite fields
entries.summary: Finite fields have prime-power size and tightly constrained multiplicative structure.

entries.title: Algebraic extensions
entries.summary: Every element of the larger field satisfies a polynomial equation over the base field.

entries.title: Galois theory
entries.summary: Automorphisms of field extensions translate polynomial questions into group-theoretic questions.

entries.title: Splitting fields
entries.summary: A splitting field is generated by all roots of a polynomial over its coefficient field.

entries.title: Group representations
entries.summary: A group acts by invertible linear transformations on a vector space.

entries.title: Irreducible representations
entries.summary: A nonzero representation has no nontrivial invariant subspace.

entries.title: Characters
entries.summary: Traces of representation matrices provide functions constant on conjugacy classes.

entries.title: Direct sums
entries.summary: Separate components combine into a larger algebraic object without interactions between summands.

entries.title: Dual representations
entries.summary: The induced action on linear functionals reverses how vectors are transformed.

entries.title: Chain complexes
entries.summary: A sequence of boundary maps has consecutive composites equal to zero.

entries.title: Exact sequences
entries.summary: At every stage, the image of the incoming map equals the kernel of the outgoing map.

entries.title: Derived functors
entries.summary: Measure the failure of a functor to preserve exactness using resolutions.

entries.title: Ext & Tor
entries.summary: Important derived functors detect extension classes and failures of tensor-product exactness.

entries.title: Elementary number theory
entries.summary: Arithmetic structure visible through divisibility, congruences, and prime factorization.

entries.title: Divisibility
entries.summary: An integer divides another when the latter is an integer multiple of the former.

entries.title: Prime numbers
entries.summary: A prime exceeds one and has exactly two positive divisors.

entries.title: Greatest common divisors
entries.summary: The largest positive common divisor organizes integer linear combinations.

entries.title: Euclidean algorithm
entries.summary: Repeated remainders efficiently compute a greatest common divisor.

entries.title: Modular arithmetic
entries.summary: Congruence identifies integers whose difference is divisible by a fixed modulus.

entries.title: Arithmetic functions
entries.summary: Functions on positive integers record divisor counts, totients, and related arithmetic information.

entries.title: Diophantine equations
entries.summary: Seek integer or rational solutions rather than arbitrary real solutions of polynomial equations.

entries.title: Chinese remainder theorem
entries.summary: Congruences with pairwise coprime moduli combine into one congruence modulo their product.

entries.title: Fermat’s little theorem
entries.summary: Exponentiation modulo a prime has a uniform constraint on nonzero residues.
entries.condition: p is prime and p does not divide a.

entries.title: Euler’s totient theorem
entries.summary: The totient counts units modulo an integer and controls a generalization of Fermat’s theorem.

entries.title: Quadratic residues
entries.summary: Ask which congruence classes can be expressed as squares modulo a given modulus.

entries.title: Quadratic reciprocity
entries.summary: Relate quadratic solvability modulo two distinct odd primes.

entries.title: Primitive roots
entries.summary: A primitive root generates the multiplicative group of units when that group is cyclic.

entries.title: Linear Diophantine equations
entries.summary: Integer solutions of ax + by = c exist exactly when gcd(a,b) divides c.

entries.title: Pell equations
entries.summary: Integer solutions of x² − Dy² = 1 connect quadratic irrationals to continued fractions.

entries.title: Pythagorean triples
entries.summary: Integer side lengths of right triangles satisfy a² + b² = c².

entries.title: Elliptic curves
entries.summary: Nonsingular cubic curves with a specified point support a geometric group law.

entries.title: Fermat’s last theorem
entries.summary: No positive integer solutions of xⁿ + yⁿ = zⁿ exist for integer n > 2.

entries.title: Analytic number theory
entries.summary: Use limits, series, and complex functions to study arithmetic patterns.

entries.title: Prime number theorem
entries.summary: The number of primes up to x is asymptotic to x/log x.
entries.condition: The ratio tends to 1 as x tends to infinity.

entries.title: Riemann zeta function
entries.summary: A Dirichlet series links complex analysis to the distribution of primes.

entries.title: Dirichlet series
entries.summary: Series indexed by n⁻ˢ encode arithmetic functions and convergence information.

entries.title: Primes in progressions
entries.summary: Every arithmetic progression with coprime starting term and step contains infinitely many primes.

entries.title: Riemann hypothesis
entries.summary: A major open conjecture places the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function on a vertical line.

entries.title: Sieve methods
entries.summary: Estimate sizes of sets after excluding integers with specified divisibility properties.

entries.title: Algebraic number theory
entries.summary: Study arithmetic in fields extending the rational numbers.

entries.title: Algebraic numbers
entries.summary: An algebraic number is a root of a nonzero polynomial with rational coefficients.

entries.title: Number fields
entries.summary: Finite extensions of the rationals supply new arithmetic environments.

entries.title: Algebraic integers
entries.summary: Roots of monic integer polynomials generalize ordinary integers inside number fields.

entries.title: Prime ideal factorization
entries.summary: Ideals can recover unique factorization when individual elements no longer factor uniquely.

entries.title: Ideal class groups
entries.summary: The class group measures the failure of principal ideals to account for all ideals.

entries.title: Valuations
entries.summary: Valuations assign sizes or orders compatible with multiplication and addition.

entries.title: Local fields
entries.summary: Locally compact fields include real, complex, and nonarchimedean examples used in arithmetic.

entries.title: Additive & geometric number theory
entries.summary: Integer sets, sums, lattice points, and geometric methods in arithmetic.

entries.title: Additive combinatorics
entries.summary: Analyze how sumsets and additive patterns constrain subsets of groups.

entries.title: Integer partitions
entries.summary: Write an integer as a sum of positive integers while ignoring summand order.

entries.title: Diophantine approximation
entries.summary: Measure how accurately real numbers can be approximated by rational numbers.

entries.title: Continued fractions
entries.summary: Nested reciprocals generate rational approximations with strong optimality properties.

entries.title: Geometry of numbers
entries.summary: Use convex bodies and lattices to solve arithmetic problems.

entries.title: Lattices
entries.summary: Discrete additive subgroups organize integer combinations of linearly independent vectors.

entries.title: Calculus
entries.summary: Differentiate to study local change, integrate to study accumulation, and use limits to connect the two.

entries.title: Single-variable calculus
entries.summary: Functions of one real variable reveal rates of change, accumulated quantities, and infinite expansions.

entries.title: Multivariable calculus
entries.summary: Generalize differentiation and integration to functions with several inputs.

entries.title: Vector calculus
entries.summary: Study scalar and vector fields through gradient, divergence, curl, and integral theorems.

entries.title: Calculus of variations
entries.summary: Optimize functionals whose unknowns are entire curves or functions.

entries.title: Limits & continuity
entries.summary: A limit describes nearby behavior; continuity matches that limit to the actual function value.

entries.title: Derivatives
entries.summary: A derivative is the limiting rate of output change per unit input change.

entries.title: Integrals
entries.summary: A definite integral measures signed accumulation and connects to antiderivatives.

entries.title: Infinite series
entries.summary: A series converges when the sequence of its partial sums approaches a finite value.

entries.title: Taylor series
entries.summary: Local derivative information forms polynomial approximations and, under convergence conditions, infinite expansions.

entries.title: Epsilon–delta definition
entries.summary: Specify a tolerance on outputs and find an input neighborhood that guarantees it.

entries.title: One-sided limits
entries.summary: Left and right approaches may behave differently near the same point.

entries.title: Squeeze theorem
entries.summary: A function trapped between two functions with the same limit shares that limit.

entries.title: Continuous functions
entries.summary: Small changes of input produce controlled changes of output near each point.

entries.title: Intermediate value theorem
entries.summary: A continuous function on an interval takes every value between two of its values.

entries.title: Extreme value theorem
entries.summary: A continuous real function on a compact nonempty interval attains a minimum and maximum.

entries.title: Differentiation rules
entries.summary: Power, product, quotient, and composition rules turn derivatives into reusable calculations.

entries.title: Chain rule
entries.summary: Differentiate a composition by composing the outer derivative and multiplying by the inner derivative.
entries.condition: Both derivatives must exist at the relevant points.

entries.title: Implicit differentiation
entries.summary: Differentiate a relation involving several variables to obtain a derivative of an implicitly defined function.

entries.title: Higher derivatives
entries.summary: Repeated differentiation measures how rates of change themselves vary.

entries.title: Mean value theorem
entries.summary: Under continuity and differentiability assumptions, an average slope occurs as a tangent slope.

entries.title: L’Hôpital’s rule
entries.summary: Certain indeterminate quotient limits can be evaluated through derivative ratios under specific hypotheses.

entries.title: Antiderivatives
entries.summary: An antiderivative differentiates to a specified function on an interval.

entries.title: Fundamental theorem of calculus
entries.summary: Differentiation and integration undo one another under appropriate regularity conditions.

entries.title: Integration by substitution
entries.summary: A change of variable transforms an integral using the chain rule in reverse.

entries.title: Integration by parts
entries.summary: Transfer a derivative from one factor to another using the product rule.

entries.title: Improper integrals
entries.summary: Infinite endpoints or unbounded integrands require an additional convergence limit.

entries.title: Riemann integration
entries.summary: Limits of partition-based sums define an integral for suitable bounded functions.

entries.title: Sequences & recurrences
entries.summary: Ordered terms can approach a limit, oscillate, or diverge according to their defining rule.

entries.title: Convergence tests
entries.summary: Comparison, ratio, root, and alternating-series tests distinguish different convergence behaviors.

entries.title: Absolute convergence
entries.summary: Convergence of the sum of absolute values is stronger than convergence of a signed series.

entries.title: Power series
entries.summary: An infinite polynomial-like expansion converges within a radius and needs separate checks at boundary points.

entries.title: Uniform convergence
entries.summary: One approximation threshold works simultaneously over the entire domain.

entries.title: Partial derivatives
entries.summary: Vary one input coordinate while holding the others fixed.

entries.title: Gradient
entries.summary: The gradient collects partial derivatives and represents directional change through an inner product.

entries.title: Jacobian
entries.summary: The derivative of a vector-valued map is represented by its matrix of first partial derivatives.

entries.title: Hessian
entries.summary: Second partial derivatives form a matrix that describes local quadratic behavior.

entries.title: Multiple integrals
entries.summary: Accumulate quantities over planar, spatial, or higher-dimensional regions.

entries.title: Change of variables
entries.summary: A Jacobian determinant corrects volume when coordinates are transformed.

entries.title: Implicit function theorem
entries.summary: A nondegenerate derivative condition lets a relation locally define some variables as functions of others.

entries.title: Divergence
entries.summary: The divergence measures local net flux per unit volume of a vector field.

entries.title: Curl
entries.summary: In three dimensions, curl measures local infinitesimal circulation.

entries.title: Line integrals
entries.summary: Integrate a scalar or vector field along a parametrized curve.

entries.title: Surface integrals
entries.summary: Integrate scalar density or oriented flux across a surface.

entries.title: Green’s theorem
entries.summary: Relate a planar boundary circulation to an integral over the enclosed region.

entries.title: Stokes’ theorem
entries.summary: Integration of an exterior derivative over a manifold matches integration over its oriented boundary.

entries.title: Divergence theorem
entries.summary: Net outward flux through a boundary equals the integral of divergence over its interior.

entries.title: Real analysis
entries.summary: Prove precise results about real functions, completeness, convergence, differentiation, and integration.

entries.title: Completeness of the reals
entries.summary: Every nonempty bounded-above set of real numbers has a real least upper bound.

entries.title: Metric spaces
entries.summary: A distance function supports limits, continuity, and Cauchy sequences without assuming coordinates.

entries.title: Cauchy sequences
entries.summary: Terms eventually become arbitrarily close to one another, whether or not a limit exists in the ambient space.

entries.title: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem
entries.summary: Every bounded sequence in finite-dimensional Euclidean space has a convergent subsequence.

entries.title: Heine–Borel theorem
entries.summary: In finite-dimensional Euclidean space, compactness is equivalent to being closed and bounded.

entries.title: Sequences of functions
entries.summary: Pointwise and uniform convergence impose different controls on limiting functions.

entries.title: Measure theory
entries.summary: Assign sizes to sets and build an integration theory that handles limits and probability robustly.

entries.title: Sigma-algebras
entries.summary: Collections of measurable sets are closed under complements and countable unions.

entries.title: Measures
entries.summary: Countable additivity assigns consistent sizes to disjoint measurable sets.

entries.title: Lebesgue measure
entries.summary: Lebesgue measure extends ordinary length, area, and volume to a broad class of sets.

entries.title: Measurable functions
entries.summary: Preimages of measurable target sets must be measurable in the source space.

entries.title: Lebesgue integration
entries.summary: Approximate measurable functions through simple functions rather than partitioning the input axis alone.

entries.title: Dominated convergence
entries.summary: An integrable dominating function allows passage of a pointwise almost-everywhere limit through an integral.

entries.title: Fubini & Tonelli theorems
entries.summary: Under integrability or nonnegativity hypotheses, product-space integrals can be iterated.

entries.title: Radon–Nikodym theorem
entries.summary: An absolutely continuous measure has a density relative to another measure under suitable finiteness assumptions.

entries.title: Complex analysis
entries.summary: Complex differentiability links local power series, contour integrals, and global geometry.

entries.title: Holomorphic functions
entries.summary: Complex differentiability on an open set imposes much stronger structure than real differentiability.

entries.title: Cauchy–Riemann equations
entries.summary: The real and imaginary parts of a holomorphic function satisfy coupled partial differential equations.

entries.title: Contour integration
entries.summary: Integrate a complex-valued function along an oriented path in the complex plane.

entries.title: Cauchy integral formula
entries.summary: Boundary values determine interior values and derivatives of a holomorphic function.

entries.title: Laurent series
entries.summary: Allow negative as well as nonnegative powers to describe functions near isolated singularities.

entries.title: Residue theorem
entries.summary: Contour integrals around isolated singularities are determined by their residue coefficients.

entries.title: Conformal maps
entries.summary: Locally angle-preserving maps connect complex analysis to planar geometry.

entries.title: Analytic continuation
entries.summary: Extend a holomorphic function beyond its initial domain through overlapping analytic representations.

entries.title: Functional analysis
entries.summary: Treat spaces of functions as geometric objects and study continuous linear operators on them.

entries.title: Normed spaces
entries.summary: A vector space with a norm combines algebraic structure with a notion of length.

entries.title: Banach spaces
entries.summary: A complete normed space contains limits of all its Cauchy sequences.

entries.title: Hilbert spaces
entries.summary: A complete inner product space extends Euclidean geometry to infinite dimensions.

entries.title: Lp spaces
entries.summary: Integrability of a power of absolute value defines important families of function spaces.

entries.title: Bounded operators
entries.summary: A linear map between normed spaces is continuous exactly when its operator norm is finite.

entries.title: Weak convergence
entries.summary: Convergence is tested through continuous linear functionals rather than through the norm directly.

entries.title: Hahn–Banach theorem
entries.summary: Extend controlled linear functionals from subspaces to larger normed spaces.

entries.title: Sobolev spaces
entries.summary: Control functions together with selected weak derivatives through integrability conditions.

entries.title: Harmonic analysis
entries.summary: Resolve functions into oscillatory components and study transformations between position and frequency.

entries.title: Fourier analysis
entries.summary: Periodic and nonperiodic functions can be analyzed through trigonometric or exponential frequency components.

entries.title: Fourier series
entries.summary: Expand a periodic function in harmonically related frequencies.

entries.title: Fourier transform
entries.summary: An integral transform expresses a function in terms of continuous frequencies.

entries.title: Convolution
entries.summary: Shift, multiply, and integrate two functions to describe smoothing and linear responses.

entries.title: Generalized functions
entries.summary: Distributions act on smooth test functions and allow differentiation beyond ordinary functions.

entries.title: Wavelets
entries.summary: Localized scale-and-position building blocks capture features at multiple resolutions.

entries.title: Special functions
entries.summary: Named function families arise repeatedly as solutions and kernels in analysis and physics.

entries.title: Gamma function
entries.summary: An integral-defined function extends factorial values to a wider domain.

entries.title: Bessel functions
entries.summary: Radial wave and diffusion equations in cylindrical coordinates lead to Bessel functions.

entries.title: Orthogonal polynomials
entries.summary: Polynomial families are orthogonal with respect to a specified weighted inner product.

entries.title: Elliptic functions
entries.summary: Meromorphic functions with two independent complex periods connect analysis to elliptic curves.

entries.title: Euclidean geometry
entries.summary: Flat spaces, straight lines, angles, congruence, and metric constructions.

entries.title: Lines & incidence
entries.summary: Incidence describes which points belong to which lines and how lines intersect.

entries.title: Triangles
entries.summary: Three-sided polygons link angle constraints, congruence, similarity, and area.

entries.title: Polygons
entries.summary: Closed chains of straight segments bound planar figures.

entries.title: Circles
entries.summary: Points at one fixed distance from a center form a circle.

entries.title: Polyhedra & solids
entries.summary: Flat polygonal faces meet along edges to form three-dimensional polyhedral surfaces.

entries.title: Trigonometry
entries.summary: Trigonometric functions connect angular position, ratios, and periodic behavior.

entries.title: Isometries
entries.summary: Distance-preserving maps express rigid geometric symmetries.

entries.title: Distance
entries.summary: A metric turns separation between points or sets into a numerical quantity.

entries.title: Angles
entries.summary: An angle measures relative direction and may be described in radians.

entries.title: Parallel lines
entries.summary: Coplanar Euclidean lines with the same direction never intersect.

entries.title: Intersections
entries.summary: Simultaneous coordinate constraints determine where geometric objects meet.

entries.title: Pythagorean theorem
entries.summary: Squared lengths in a right triangle obey a fundamental Euclidean identity.
entries.condition: c is the hypotenuse of a Euclidean right triangle.

entries.title: Similarity & congruence
entries.summary: Similarity preserves shape up to scale; congruence also preserves all distances.

entries.title: Triangle centers
entries.summary: Centroid, circumcenter, incenter, and orthocenter arise from different canonical constructions.

entries.title: Law of cosines
entries.summary: An included angle determines the relation between all three side lengths.
entries.condition: γ is the angle between sides a and b.

entries.title: Arcs & sectors
entries.summary: Angle and radius determine circular arc length and sector area.

entries.title: Tangents to circles
entries.summary: A tangent line meets a circle once and is perpendicular to its radius at the contact point.

entries.title: Inscribed angles
entries.summary: Central and inscribed angles subtending the same arc are related by a factor of two.

entries.title: Prisms
entries.summary: Congruent parallel polygonal bases are connected by parallelogram faces.

entries.title: Pyramids
entries.summary: A polygonal base joins to an apex through triangular faces.

entries.title: Platonic solids
entries.summary: Five convex regular polyhedra have congruent regular faces and identical vertex figures.

entries.title: Hypercubes
entries.summary: The Cartesian product of intervals generalizes a square and cube to any finite dimension.

entries.title: Simplices
entries.summary: An n-simplex is the convex hull of n + 1 affinely independent points.

entries.title: Hyperspheres
entries.summary: Points at a fixed distance from a center form a sphere in higher-dimensional Euclidean space.

entries.title: Affine & projective geometry
entries.summary: Study properties preserved by affine or projective changes of coordinates.

entries.title: Affine spaces
entries.summary: Differences of points are vectors, while no origin is distinguished.

entries.title: Projective spaces
entries.summary: One-dimensional linear subspaces become points in a space that incorporates directions at infinity.

entries.title: Homogeneous coordinates
entries.summary: Coordinates differing by a nonzero common factor describe the same projective point.

entries.title: Conic sections
entries.summary: Quadratic plane curves include ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.

entries.title: Cross-ratio
entries.summary: A ratio built from four collinear points is preserved by projective transformations.

entries.title: Projective duality
entries.summary: Points and hyperplanes can exchange roles in incidence statements.

entries.title: Non-Euclidean geometry
entries.summary: Replace Euclid’s parallel postulate and examine geometries with different curvature and incidence behavior.

entries.title: Hyperbolic geometry
entries.summary: Constant negative curvature leads to distinctive triangles, distances, and parallel lines.

entries.title: Spherical geometry
entries.summary: Great-circle arcs supply natural geodesics on a sphere.

entries.title: Geodesics
entries.summary: A geodesic is a locally straight path relative to a space’s metric connection.

entries.title: Parallel postulates
entries.summary: Changing the Euclidean parallel condition produces fundamentally different geometries.

entries.title: Tessellations
entries.summary: Tiles cover a surface without gaps or overlaps in their interiors.

entries.title: Poincaré disk
entries.summary: A disk models the hyperbolic plane with angle-preserving coordinates.

entries.title: Hyperbolic triangles
entries.summary: A hyperbolic triangle has angle sum smaller than π radians.

entries.title: Horocycles
entries.summary: A limit of suitable hyperbolic circles shares a point at infinity.

entries.title: Hyperbolic spaces
entries.summary: Complete simply connected spaces of constant negative sectional curvature generalize the hyperbolic plane.

entries.title: Great circles
entries.summary: A plane through the sphere’s center cuts out its geodesic circles.

entries.title: Spherical triangles
entries.summary: A nondegenerate spherical geodesic triangle has angle sum larger than π radians.

entries.title: Spherical spaces
entries.summary: Positive constant-curvature spaces provide the spherical counterpart of Euclidean and hyperbolic geometry.

entries.title: Differential geometry
entries.summary: Use derivatives and smooth coordinates to study the local and global geometry of spaces.

entries.title: Curves & surfaces
entries.summary: Tangents, normals, and curvature describe smooth embedded geometric objects.

entries.title: Smooth manifolds
entries.summary: Compatible charts make a space locally resemble Euclidean space with smooth coordinate changes.

entries.title: Tangent spaces
entries.summary: Velocities of curves through a point form its linear space of infinitesimal directions.

entries.title: Differential forms
entries.summary: Alternating covariant tensors provide coordinate-independent objects for integration.

entries.title: Riemannian geometry
entries.summary: A smoothly varying positive-definite inner product measures lengths and angles on a manifold.

entries.title: Symplectic geometry
entries.summary: A closed nondegenerate two-form supplies the geometry of Hamiltonian phase spaces.

entries.title: Metric tensors
entries.summary: A metric assigns a bilinear measurement rule to each tangent space.

entries.title: Connections & covariant derivatives
entries.summary: A connection differentiates vector fields and compares directions at nearby points.

entries.title: Levi-Civita connection
entries.summary: A Riemannian metric determines a unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection.

entries.title: Curvature tensors
entries.summary: Curvature measures the failure of successive covariant derivatives to commute.

entries.title: Parallel transport
entries.summary: A connection carries tangent vectors along paths while preserving a notion of parallelism.

entries.title: Gauss–Bonnet theorem
entries.summary: Integrated curvature relates to the topology of a compact surface.

entries.title: Geometric flows
entries.summary: Evolution equations deform metrics, embeddings, or connections according to geometric quantities.

entries.title: Ricci flow
entries.summary: A metric evolves in a direction controlled by its Ricci curvature.
entries.condition: This is the unnormalized Ricci flow; singularities may develop.

entries.title: Mean curvature flow
entries.summary: An immersed submanifold moves in the direction of its mean curvature vector.

entries.title: Algebraic geometry
entries.summary: Translate polynomial equations into geometric spaces and geometric questions into algebra.

entries.title: Algebraic varieties
entries.summary: Common zeros of polynomial equations form algebraic geometric objects.

entries.title: Coordinate rings
entries.summary: Polynomial functions on an affine algebraic set form a ring encoding its geometry.

entries.title: Hilbert’s Nullstellensatz
entries.summary: Over an algebraically closed field, ideals and common zero sets are linked through radicals.

entries.title: Morphisms & rational maps
entries.summary: Regular and rational maps express different notions of algebraic geometric transformation.

entries.title: Schemes
entries.summary: Glue spectra of commutative rings to generalize varieties and retain arithmetic information.

entries.title: Sheaves
entries.summary: Compatible local data can be glued into global data on a topological space or site.

entries.title: Singularities
entries.summary: Algebraic spaces can fail to be smooth at points with degenerate local behavior.
entries.sourceTitle: Singular point of an algebraic variety

entries.title: Affine varieties
entries.summary: Polynomial zero sets live inside affine space over a chosen field.

entries.title: Projective varieties
entries.summary: Homogeneous polynomial equations define zero sets in projective space.

entries.title: Algebraic curves
entries.summary: One-dimensional algebraic varieties connect polynomial equations to complex and arithmetic geometry.

entries.title: Convex & discrete geometry
entries.summary: Study convex bodies, finite configurations, arrangements, and extremal geometric structures.

entries.title: Convex sets
entries.summary: Every line segment between two points of a convex set stays in the set.

entries.title: Convex hulls
entries.summary: The smallest convex set containing given points consists of their convex combinations.

entries.title: Polytopes
entries.summary: Higher-dimensional convex polytopes connect geometry, inequalities, and combinatorics.

entries.title: Voronoi diagrams
entries.summary: Partition a metric space according to which designated site is nearest.

entries.title: Sphere packing
entries.summary: Arrange nonoverlapping equal spheres and ask how dense the arrangement can be.

entries.title: General topology
entries.summary: Open sets define continuity and local structure without requiring a distance formula.

entries.title: Topological spaces
entries.summary: A collection of open sets satisfies closure rules for unions and finite intersections.

entries.title: Open & closed sets
entries.summary: Openness is part of a topology, while a closed set has an open complement.

entries.title: Neighborhoods & bases
entries.summary: A basis generates all open sets from simpler local pieces.

entries.title: Continuity & homeomorphism
entries.summary: A continuous bijection with continuous inverse identifies topological spaces.

entries.title: Compactness
entries.summary: Every open cover of a compact space has a finite subcover.

entries.title: Connectedness
entries.summary: A connected space cannot be split into two disjoint nonempty open pieces.

entries.title: Separation axioms
entries.summary: Axioms such as Hausdorffness specify how points and sets can be distinguished by neighborhoods.

entries.title: Products & quotients
entries.summary: Product and quotient constructions create topologies compatible with specified maps.

entries.title: Algebraic topology
entries.summary: Algebraic invariants detect and organize topological shapes and their holes.

entries.title: Homotopy
entries.summary: A continuous deformation between maps compares them without demanding exact equality.

entries.title: Fundamental groups
entries.summary: Loops based at a point form a group under concatenation up to homotopy.

entries.title: Covering spaces
entries.summary: A map locally resembles several separate copies of its target neighborhood.

entries.title: Homology
entries.summary: Cycles modulo boundaries encode holes in different dimensions.

entries.title: Cohomology
entries.summary: Dual algebraic constructions add operations and further structure to topological invariants.

entries.title: Euler characteristic
entries.summary: An alternating count of cells or homological ranks is a fundamental topological invariant.

entries.title: Higher homotopy groups
entries.summary: Maps from higher-dimensional spheres extend the loop-based idea of the fundamental group.

entries.title: Simplicial complexes
entries.summary: Vertices, edges, triangles, and their higher-dimensional analogues assemble into combinatorial spaces.

entries.title: Singular homology
entries.summary: Continuous maps from simplices define chains on very general topological spaces.

entries.title: Persistent homology
entries.summary: Track topological features across a changing scale or filtration.

entries.title: Differential topology
entries.summary: Study smooth manifolds and maps through properties unaffected by smooth coordinate changes.

entries.title: Tangent bundles
entries.summary: All tangent spaces of a manifold assemble into a larger smooth space.

entries.title: Vector bundles
entries.summary: A family of vector spaces varies locally like a product over a base space.

entries.title: Transversality
entries.summary: Submanifolds or maps meet with tangent directions in sufficiently general position.

entries.title: Sard’s theorem
entries.summary: Critical values of a sufficiently differentiable map form a measure-zero set.

entries.title: Morse theory
entries.summary: Critical points of smooth functions reveal how a manifold is assembled.

entries.title: Cobordism
entries.summary: Two manifolds can be related as boundary components of a higher-dimensional manifold.

entries.title: Geometric topology
entries.summary: Study manifolds, embeddings, knots, and low-dimensional geometric structure.

entries.title: Classification of surfaces
entries.summary: Compact surfaces are classified through orientability and genus with appropriate boundary data.

entries.title: Knot theory
entries.summary: Embeddings of circles in three-dimensional space can be distinguished by topological invariants.

entries.title: Three-manifolds
entries.summary: Three-dimensional spaces admit particularly rich decomposition and geometric theories.

entries.title: Geometrization
entries.summary: Closed three-manifolds can be decomposed into pieces with canonical geometric structures.

entries.title: Fixed-point theorems
entries.summary: Topological conditions can guarantee a map has a point that it leaves unchanged.

entries.title: Combinatorics
entries.summary: Count configurations, prove they exist, and understand how discrete structures fit together.

entries.title: Counting principles
entries.summary: Addition and multiplication rules count alternatives and successive choices.

entries.title: Permutations
entries.summary: An ordered arrangement differs from an unordered selection.

entries.title: Combinations
entries.summary: Count subsets of a prescribed size without regard to order.

entries.title: Inclusion–exclusion
entries.summary: Alternating intersection counts correct overcounting in a union.

entries.title: Pigeonhole principle
entries.summary: More objects than containers force at least one container to contain multiple objects.

entries.title: Generating functions
entries.summary: Coefficients of formal or convergent power series encode combinatorial sequences.

entries.title: Recurrence relations
entries.summary: Later terms depend on earlier terms through a specified relation and initial data.

entries.title: Extremal combinatorics
entries.summary: Ask how large a discrete structure can be while avoiding a forbidden configuration.

entries.title: Ramsey theory
entries.summary: Sufficiently large structures force organized substructures despite arbitrary colorings.

entries.title: Probabilistic method
entries.summary: Show a desired object exists by proving a randomly chosen object can have the required property.

entries.title: Graph theory
entries.summary: Vertices and edges describe connectivity, routes, constraints, and finite networks.

entries.title: Graphs & degree
entries.summary: A vertex’s degree counts incident edges, with loops counted twice in undirected graphs.

entries.title: Paths & cycles
entries.summary: Paths follow successive edges; cycles return to their starting point without repeated intermediate vertices.

entries.title: Trees & forests
entries.summary: Connected acyclic graphs are trees; collections of trees form forests.

entries.title: Graph connectivity
entries.summary: Connectivity measures whether and how robustly vertices remain linked by paths.

entries.title: Graph coloring
entries.summary: Assign colors subject to adjacency constraints on vertices, edges, or other graph objects.

entries.title: Planar graphs
entries.summary: A planar graph can be drawn in the plane with no edge crossings except at shared endpoints.

entries.title: Matchings
entries.summary: A matching chooses edges without shared endpoints.

entries.title: Network flows
entries.summary: Flows satisfy capacity constraints and conservation through an oriented network.

entries.title: Random graphs
entries.summary: Probability models on graphs reveal typical and threshold behavior of networks.

entries.title: Spectral graph theory
entries.summary: Matrix spectra reveal connectivity, expansion, and other graph properties.

entries.title: Spanning trees
entries.summary: A spanning tree connects every vertex of a connected graph using no cycles.

entries.title: Rooted trees
entries.summary: Distinguishing a root turns a tree into a hierarchy with parent and child directions.

entries.title: Minimum spanning trees
entries.summary: Choose a spanning tree whose total edge weight is as small as possible.

entries.title: Order theory
entries.summary: Comparability, hierarchy, and lattice structure organize discrete and continuous mathematical objects.

entries.title: Partial orders
entries.summary: Reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive relations permit some pairs to remain incomparable.

entries.title: Hasse diagrams
entries.summary: Show cover relations of a finite partial order while omitting relations forced by transitivity.

entries.title: Order lattices
entries.summary: Pairs of elements have greatest lower bounds and least upper bounds.

entries.title: Boolean algebra
entries.summary: Complement, meet, and join abstract the algebra of logical truth and set operations.

entries.title: Möbius inversion
entries.summary: Invert cumulative sums on divisibility orders or more general locally finite partial orders.

entries.title: Designs & matroids
entries.summary: Study balanced incidence patterns and abstract notions of independence.

entries.title: Combinatorial designs
entries.summary: Arrange subsets so that specified incidences occur in a balanced, controlled way.

entries.title: Latin squares
entries.summary: Each symbol appears exactly once in each row and column of a square array.

entries.title: Finite geometries
entries.summary: Incidence geometries with finitely many points link combinatorics to finite fields.

entries.title: Matroids
entries.summary: Independence axioms generalize linear independence and cycle-free subsets of graph edges.

entries.title: Enumerative combinatorics
entries.summary: Count structures using recurrences, bijections, generating functions, and algebraic methods.

entries.title: Probability foundations
entries.summary: A probability space combines possible outcomes, measurable events, and a normalized measure.

entries.title: Events & probability
entries.summary: Events are measurable sets of outcomes; their probabilities obey countable additivity.

entries.title: Probability axioms
entries.summary: Nonnegativity, normalization, and countable additivity constrain every probability model.

entries.title: Independence
entries.summary: Joint probabilities factor when events or variables are independent.

entries.title: Conditional probability
entries.summary: Restrict probability to outcomes consistent with an event of positive probability.

entries.title: Bayes’ theorem
entries.summary: Reverse conditional probabilities by combining likelihoods, priors, and marginal probabilities.

entries.title: Conditional expectation
entries.summary: A measurable projection expresses the best available expectation given specified information.

entries.title: Random variables & distributions
entries.summary: Random variables turn outcomes into numbers; distributions describe their probabilities.

entries.title: Discrete distributions
entries.summary: Probability masses assign weights to countably many possible values.

entries.title: Continuous distributions
entries.summary: A density describes probability through integrals over sets rather than values at isolated points.

entries.title: Expectation
entries.summary: An integrable random variable has a probability-weighted average.

entries.title: Variance & covariance
entries.summary: Second moments quantify spread and joint linear variation.

entries.title: Joint distributions
entries.summary: Describe several random variables together, retaining their dependence.

entries.title: Characteristic functions
entries.summary: Expected complex exponentials uniquely encode probability distributions.

entries.title: Bernoulli distribution
entries.summary: One binary trial assigns probabilities p and 1 − p to two outcomes.

entries.title: Binomial distribution
entries.summary: Count successes in a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials with common success probability.

entries.title: Poisson distribution
entries.summary: A nonnegative count distribution models independent events at a fixed average rate in standard Poisson settings.

entries.title: Geometric distribution
entries.summary: Count trials until a first success, or failures before it, depending on the stated convention.

entries.title: Uniform distribution
entries.summary: A constant density assigns equal probability to equal-length subintervals within its support.

entries.title: Normal distribution
entries.summary: A mean and positive variance specify the familiar symmetric bell-shaped density.

entries.title: Exponential distribution
entries.summary: A memoryless positive waiting time is parametrized by a positive rate.

entries.title: Gamma distribution
entries.summary: Shape and rate or scale parameters generalize exponential waiting-time distributions.

entries.title: Beta distribution
entries.summary: A flexible density on the unit interval is useful for uncertain proportions.

entries.title: Limit theorems
entries.summary: Different modes of convergence explain stable averages and universal limiting distributions.

entries.title: Modes of convergence
entries.summary: Almost sure, in-probability, distributional, and Lp convergence express different limiting requirements.

entries.title: Law of large numbers
entries.summary: Under suitable assumptions, sample averages converge to an expected value.

entries.title: Central limit theorem
entries.summary: Properly centered and scaled sums often approach a normal distribution under suitable conditions.

entries.title: Concentration inequalities
entries.summary: Bounds quantify how unlikely a random variable is to deviate far from its typical value.

entries.title: Large deviations
entries.summary: Study exponential-scale probabilities of unusually large fluctuations.

entries.title: Stochastic processes
entries.summary: Collections of random variables describe evolving random systems across time or another index.

entries.title: Markov chains
entries.summary: Given the present state, earlier states provide no additional information about the next transition.

entries.title: Poisson processes
entries.summary: Independent increments with Poisson counts model arrivals under a constant-rate homogeneous model.

entries.title: Martingales
entries.summary: Conditional expected future value equals the current value under the defining integrability assumptions.

entries.title: Brownian motion
entries.summary: A continuous process with independent Gaussian increments is a central model of random fluctuation.

entries.title: Stationary processes
entries.summary: Distributional properties are invariant under shifts of the time index in the relevant sense of stationarity.

entries.title: Ergodic theory
entries.summary: Invariant measures connect long-time averages with space averages for suitable dynamical systems.

entries.title: Stochastic calculus
entries.summary: Develop integration and differential equations driven by irregular random processes.

entries.title: Itô integral
entries.summary: Construct stochastic integrals of adapted integrands against processes such as Brownian motion.

entries.title: Itô’s lemma
entries.summary: A stochastic chain rule includes a second-derivative correction from quadratic variation.

entries.title: Stochastic differential equations
entries.summary: Differential models combine drift with a stochastic driving term.

entries.title: Diffusion processes
entries.summary: Continuous random evolution connects stochastic equations to second-order differential operators.

entries.title: Descriptive statistics
entries.summary: Summarize the center, variation, and shape of observed data without hiding the data-generating context.

entries.title: Mean, median & mode
entries.summary: Different notions of a typical value react differently to skew, outliers, and data type.

entries.title: Variance & spread
entries.summary: Spread summaries compare the variability of observations around a center.

entries.title: Quantiles
entries.summary: Quantiles split an ordered distribution into prescribed probability portions.

entries.title: Correlation
entries.summary: Correlation measures selected forms of association and does not by itself establish causation.

entries.title: Empirical distributions
entries.summary: A sample defines a distribution by placing equal mass on each observed value.

entries.title: Statistical inference
entries.summary: Use sample data and assumptions to estimate unknown features of a population or model.

entries.title: Sampling & estimation
entries.summary: A sampling mechanism determines how observations represent a target population.

entries.title: Estimators
entries.summary: An estimator is a statistic used to infer an unknown parameter.

entries.title: Bias & variance of estimators
entries.summary: Bias and sampling variability capture different sources of estimation error.

entries.title: Likelihood
entries.summary: Treat the probability model of observed data as a function of its unknown parameters.

entries.title: Maximum likelihood
entries.summary: Choose parameter values that maximize the observed-data likelihood.

entries.title: Confidence intervals
entries.summary: Repeated-sampling coverage is a property of the interval-producing procedure.

entries.title: Sufficient statistics
entries.summary: A statistic retains all information in the sample about a parameter under a specified model.

entries.title: Sampling bias
entries.summary: Systematic differences between inclusion and exclusion can distort an estimate regardless of sample size.

entries.title: Bootstrap methods
entries.summary: Resampling from an empirical distribution approximates selected sampling properties of a statistic.

entries.title: Standard errors
entries.summary: A standard error describes the sampling variability of an estimator, rather than the spread of individual data values.

entries.title: Hypothesis testing
entries.summary: Evaluate how observations compare with predictions of a specified null model.

entries.title: Null & alternative hypotheses
entries.summary: State the competing model claims before choosing a test and interpreting its result.

entries.title: P-values
entries.summary: A p-value evaluates a specified extremeness event under the null model, not the probability that the null is true.

entries.title: Type I & II errors
entries.summary: Rejecting a true null and failing to reject a false null are distinct errors.
entries.sourceTitle: Type I and type II errors

entries.title: Statistical power
entries.summary: Power is the rejection probability under a specified alternative data-generating process.

entries.title: t-tests
entries.summary: Studentized statistics compare means under the assumptions of the chosen test variant.

entries.title: Chi-squared tests
entries.summary: Observed and expected counts can be compared with a chi-squared reference approximation under suitable assumptions.

entries.title: Multiple testing
entries.summary: Performing many tests requires an explicit choice of familywise or false-discovery error control.

entries.title: Regression & models
entries.summary: Model conditional outcomes, estimate relationships, and examine the assumptions behind predictions.

entries.title: Linear regression
entries.summary: A response is modeled as a linear combination of predictors with an error structure.

entries.title: Least squares
entries.summary: Minimize squared residuals to fit an approximation or a statistical model.

entries.title: Logistic regression
entries.summary: A logistic link relates predictors to the probability of a binary outcome.

entries.title: Generalized linear models
entries.summary: A link function and exponential-family response model extend ordinary linear regression.

entries.title: Regularization
entries.summary: Penalties or constraints control model complexity and stabilize estimation.

entries.title: Model selection
entries.summary: Compare candidate models using predictive assessment, information criteria, or other justified objectives.

entries.title: Bayesian statistics
entries.summary: Combine a prior distribution with a likelihood to obtain a posterior distribution.

entries.title: Priors & posteriors
entries.summary: The posterior describes uncertainty about model quantities after conditioning on the observed data.

entries.title: Conjugate priors
entries.summary: A conjugate prior family retains its functional form after a specified likelihood update.

entries.title: Credible intervals
entries.summary: A credible region contains a stated amount of posterior probability under a Bayesian model.

entries.title: Markov chain Monte Carlo
entries.summary: A suitably designed Markov chain supplies samples for approximating a target distribution.

entries.title: Bayes factors
entries.summary: Ratios of marginal likelihoods compare how models predict the observed data.

entries.title: Multivariate & experimental methods
entries.summary: Study interacting variables, dependence over time, and designs that support interpretable comparisons.

entries.title: Analysis of variance
entries.summary: Partition variation to compare model components or group means under an explicit error model.

entries.title: Experimental design
entries.summary: Randomization, blocking, and replication determine what comparisons data can support.

entries.title: Causal inference
entries.summary: Causal claims need assumptions or designs beyond observed association alone.

entries.title: Principal component analysis
entries.summary: Orthogonal directions capture successive amounts of variance in centered multivariate data.

entries.title: Time series
entries.summary: Temporal ordering introduces serial dependence, trends, and dynamic structure into observations.

entries.title: Nonparametric statistics
entries.summary: Statistical procedures avoid restricting the model to a fixed finite-dimensional parameter family.

entries.title: Ordinary differential equations
entries.summary: Unknown functions of one independent variable are constrained by their derivatives.

entries.title: First-order ODEs
entries.summary: The highest derivative is first order, with a derivative prescribed through the current state and input.

entries.title: Linear ODEs
entries.summary: The unknown function and its derivatives appear linearly, enabling superposition for homogeneous equations.

entries.title: Systems of ODEs
entries.summary: Several coupled unknown functions evolve together as a vector-valued system.

entries.title: Existence & uniqueness
entries.summary: Regularity assumptions give local existence and uniqueness for initial-value problems.

entries.title: Boundary-value problems
entries.summary: Constraints at different endpoints replace or supplement initial data.

entries.title: Laplace transform
entries.summary: An integral transform turns many linear differential equations into algebraic relations.

entries.title: Separable equations
entries.summary: Separate dependent and independent factors, integrate, and check excluded equilibrium solutions.

entries.title: Integrating factors
entries.summary: Multiplying by a suitable function turns certain equations into an exact derivative.

entries.title: Exact differential equations
entries.summary: A differential form comes from a potential function when the relevant exactness conditions hold.

entries.title: Partial differential equations
entries.summary: Derivatives with respect to several independent variables describe fields and spatial evolution.

entries.title: PDE classification
entries.summary: Elliptic, parabolic, and hyperbolic types indicate different geometric and propagation behavior.

entries.title: Laplace & Poisson equations
entries.summary: Elliptic equations describe harmonic potentials and responses to source terms.

entries.title: Heat equation
entries.summary: A parabolic equation models diffusion and the smoothing of spatial variation.

entries.title: Wave equation
entries.summary: A hyperbolic equation models finite-speed propagation of disturbances.

entries.title: Transport equations
entries.summary: First-order field equations carry quantities along a prescribed flow.

entries.title: Navier–Stokes equations
entries.summary: Velocity and pressure fields describe viscous fluid motion under continuum assumptions.

entries.title: Weak solutions
entries.summary: An integral or distributional formulation permits solutions lacking classical derivatives.

entries.title: Method of characteristics
entries.summary: Follow special curves that reduce suitable first-order PDEs to ordinary differential equations.

entries.title: Dynamical systems
entries.summary: Maps and flows organize the qualitative behavior of evolving states.

entries.title: Phase space
entries.summary: Each point records a complete state; trajectories trace its evolution.

entries.title: Equilibria & fixed points
entries.summary: An equilibrium state does not change under the governing evolution.

entries.title: Stability theory
entries.summary: Ask whether small perturbations remain small, decay, or grow.

entries.title: Lyapunov functions
entries.summary: A scalar function with controlled change along trajectories can establish stability.

entries.title: Bifurcation theory
entries.summary: Qualitative dynamics change as model parameters cross special values.

entries.title: Chaos theory
entries.summary: Deterministic evolution can show complex long-term behavior and sensitivity to initial conditions.

entries.title: Attractors
entries.summary: Trajectories from a surrounding region approach an invariant set in a specified sense.

entries.title: Control theory
entries.summary: Design inputs and feedback to influence the behavior of dynamical systems.

entries.title: State-space models
entries.summary: Matrices describe linear state dynamics, inputs, and observed outputs.

entries.title: Controllability
entries.summary: Ask which states can be reached by suitable admissible inputs.

entries.title: Observability
entries.summary: Ask whether internal states can be reconstructed from output information.

entries.title: Feedback control
entries.summary: Use measured behavior to adjust an input and influence future system evolution.

entries.title: Optimal control
entries.summary: Choose a time-dependent input minimizing a cost while obeying dynamical constraints.

entries.title: Convex optimization
