entries.summary: Convex feasible sets and convex objectives permit strong global guarantees and useful dual problems.

entries.title: Convex functions
entries.summary: The function’s value on a segment lies below the corresponding weighted average of endpoint values.

entries.title: Convex programs
entries.summary: Minimize a convex objective over a convex feasible set.

entries.title: Lagrange multipliers
entries.summary: At a regular constrained extremum, objective and constraint gradients satisfy a compatibility condition.

entries.title: Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions
entries.summary: Stationarity, feasibility, and complementary slackness describe constrained candidates under suitable assumptions.

entries.title: Optimization duality
entries.summary: A related optimization problem produces bounds and sometimes exactly the same optimal value.

entries.title: Gradient descent
entries.summary: Take iterative steps against the gradient to reduce a differentiable objective under appropriate step-size conditions.

entries.title: Interior-point methods
entries.summary: Barrier-based iterations solve constrained programs while approaching an optimum through the interior.

entries.title: Mathematical programming
entries.summary: Express optimization tasks through variables, an objective, and explicit constraints.

entries.title: Linear programming
entries.summary: Optimize a linear function over a set described by linear equality and inequality constraints.

entries.title: Simplex method
entries.summary: Move between vertices of a feasible polyhedron to improve a linear objective.

entries.title: Integer programming
entries.summary: Require some decision variables to be integers, introducing discrete feasibility constraints.

entries.title: Quadratic programming
entries.summary: A quadratic objective is optimized under prescribed constraints.

entries.title: Nonlinear programming
entries.summary: Objectives or constraints may be nonlinear, so local and global solutions must be distinguished.

entries.title: Dynamic programming
entries.summary: Decompose an optimization problem into overlapping subproblems with reusable optimal values.

entries.title: Game theory
entries.summary: Study decisions whose outcomes depend on the interacting choices of several agents.

entries.title: Strategic-form games
entries.summary: Specify agents, strategy sets, and payoffs for every joint strategy choice.

entries.title: Nash equilibrium
entries.summary: No player can improve its payoff by changing strategy alone while the others hold theirs fixed.

entries.title: Zero-sum games
entries.summary: One player’s gain exactly offsets the other player’s loss.

entries.title: Minimax theorem
entries.summary: Under suitable assumptions, optimal worst-case and best-response values coincide.

entries.title: Cooperative games
entries.summary: Coalitions and transferable or nontransferable payoffs describe cooperation among agents.

entries.title: Mechanism design
entries.summary: Design interaction rules so agents’ incentives support a desired outcome.

entries.title: Operations research
entries.summary: Allocate scarce resources and coordinate systems using mathematical models and algorithms.

entries.title: Queueing theory
entries.summary: Random arrivals, service, and congestion determine waiting times and system occupancy.

entries.title: Scheduling theory
entries.summary: Allocate jobs to resources across time under precedence and capacity constraints.

entries.title: Inventory theory
entries.summary: Balance ordering, holding, and shortage costs under uncertainty and demand constraints.

entries.title: Transportation problems
entries.summary: Find efficient assignments of mass or goods from sources to destinations.

entries.title: Optimal transport
entries.summary: Compare and transform probability measures by minimizing a transport cost.

entries.title: Decision theory
entries.summary: Evaluate actions through preferences, information, uncertainty, and a loss or utility model.

entries.title: Algorithms
entries.summary: Finite procedures need precise inputs, outputs, correctness arguments, and resource bounds.

entries.title: Correctness & invariants
entries.summary: An invariant stays true through an iteration and can support a proof of algorithmic correctness.

entries.title: Divide & conquer
entries.summary: Split a task into smaller instances, solve them, and combine the results.

entries.title: Greedy algorithms
entries.summary: Choose locally favorable actions; special structure is needed for global optimality.

entries.title: Graph algorithms
entries.summary: Traverse and analyze finite networks to answer reachability, distance, and structural questions.

entries.title: Randomized algorithms
entries.summary: Random choices can simplify a procedure or improve expected resource use.

entries.title: Symbolic computation
entries.summary: Manipulate exact expressions such as polynomials and rational functions rather than only numeric approximations.

entries.title: Computational complexity
entries.summary: Study resource requirements of computational problems as input size grows.

entries.title: Asymptotic notation
entries.summary: Upper, lower, and tight asymptotic bounds compare growth while suppressing fixed constants.

entries.title: P, NP & NP-completeness
entries.summary: Distinguish efficiently solvable problems from efficiently verifiable ones and the hardest problems within NP.

entries.title: Computational reductions
entries.summary: Transform one problem into another to compare their computational difficulty.

entries.title: Space complexity
entries.summary: Memory requirements provide a different resource measure from execution time.

entries.title: Approximation algorithms
entries.summary: Prove quantitative quality guarantees when an exact optimum is computationally difficult to obtain.

entries.title: Computability
entries.summary: Some precisely described decision problems cannot be solved by any general terminating algorithm.

entries.title: Turing machines
entries.summary: An idealized machine formalizes a general notion of effective symbolic computation.

entries.title: Halting problem
entries.summary: No algorithm can decide termination correctly for every program and input.

entries.title: Decidability
entries.summary: A decision problem is decidable when one algorithm always halts with the correct yes-or-no answer.

entries.title: Automata theory
entries.summary: Finite and other restricted machines characterize classes of formal languages.

entries.title: Recursive functions
entries.summary: Function-building rules provide a formal model equivalent in power to Turing computation.

entries.title: Numerical analysis
entries.summary: Approximate mathematical problems while controlling discretization, conditioning, stability, and rounding error.

entries.title: Errors & floating point
entries.summary: Finite representations introduce rounding; numerical errors must be distinguished from modeling and truncation errors.

entries.title: Conditioning & stability
entries.summary: Conditioning concerns sensitivity of a problem; stability concerns the behavior of a chosen algorithm.

entries.title: Root finding
entries.summary: Iterative methods locate values at which a function vanishes.

entries.title: Interpolation
entries.summary: Construct a function matching prescribed values at specified nodes.

entries.title: Numerical integration
entries.summary: Weighted function evaluations approximate an integral with a quantifiable error model.

entries.title: Numerical linear algebra
entries.summary: Stable factorizations and iterative methods solve large linear algebra problems.

entries.title: Numerical differential equations
entries.summary: Time stepping or spatial discretization turns differential models into finite computations.
entries.sourceTitle: Numerical methods for ordinary differential equations

entries.title: Bisection method

entries.title: Newton’s method
entries.summary: A tangent-line correction refines a root estimate when the derivative and convergence conditions cooperate.

entries.title: Secant method
entries.summary: Approximate a derivative from previous function values to generate a root-finding iteration.

entries.title: Gaussian elimination
entries.summary: Elementary row operations reduce a linear system; pivoting helps manage numerical stability.

entries.title: Iterative linear solvers
entries.summary: Successive approximations solve systems without requiring an explicit matrix inverse.

entries.title: Conjugate gradients
entries.summary: Exploit positive-definite symmetric structure through mutually conjugate search directions.

entries.title: Eigenvalue algorithms
entries.summary: Numerical iterations approximate spectral values and invariant subspaces.

entries.title: Euler method
entries.summary: A first-order step follows the current derivative over a short interval.

entries.title: Runge–Kutta methods
entries.summary: Several derivative evaluations combine into a higher-order time step.

entries.title: Finite differences
entries.summary: Approximate derivatives by differences on a grid to obtain algebraic equations.

entries.title: Finite elements
entries.summary: Piecewise basis functions approximate weak formulations on a partitioned domain.

entries.title: Spectral methods
entries.summary: Global basis expansions approximate functions and differential operators with high accuracy for smooth problems.

entries.title: Information theory
entries.summary: Quantify uncertainty and the limits of communication and lossless or lossy representation.

entries.title: Shannon entropy
entries.summary: Expected information content quantifies uncertainty in a discrete random variable.

entries.title: Mutual information
